text:
Brandon Montour plays more than anyone on the Kraken blue line, 24:22 a night, and he has 16 points in 22 games. This week his name was in the headlines for something bigger than hockey: he and Adam Fox teamed up on an effort to fight ALS across the league, as NHL.com reported.

On the ice, the picture is mixed. He is producing at 1.79 points per 60 minutes, above the top of our talent range, and a big part of that is the people around him: Seattle has scored 7.4 more goals than its chances deserve with him on. His own shooting has been quiet, no goals in his last ten games and only about one expected goal in that span, though he still has the 97th percentile shot speed that made him a Cup winner with Florida in 2024.

The encouraging part is relative. Seattle's share of chances is almost five points better with him on the ice than without him, and Evolving-Hockey noted last season that he plays with weaker teammates than most. The thing to watch is his shot: 43 in 22 games, with not much getting through lately.
